With a parameter vector $\vparam$,
the normalizing constant of the posterior is

$$\p(\vy) = \int_{\Paramspace} \p(\vy \mid \vparam)\, \p(\vparam)\, d\vparam,$$

an integral over the [parameter space](#def-parameter-space) $\Paramspace$,
which spans every dimension of $\vparam$,
that typically has no closed form.
Computing it numerically becomes infeasible as the dimension of $\vparam$ grows
[@dobson4e, Chapter 13, p. 287].
MCMC sidesteps the problem:
MCMC samplers use the posterior only through ratios
$\p(\vparam^* \mid \vy) / \p(\vparam \mid \vy)$,
in which the normalizing constant cancels.
